title: Initial evaluation, neck after car accident, dizziness

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Hi Sam. It's been a month since your car accident. How is the neck now?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Neck pain is about 6 out of 10 on the left side. It's worse when I turn to check mirrors.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I've also had dizziness when I stand up quickly, twice this week.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Thank you for telling me. Any numbness or tingling down the arms?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Some tingling in my left pinky, a couple of times.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Any trouble swallowing, vision changes, or new headaches?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No swallowing trouble. Vision is fine. Headaches are the same as before.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Let me measure rotation. Turning to the left is about 40 degrees, and to the right 60.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Driving is hard because I can't look over my shoulder.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Assessment: the neck is stiff on the left, and the dizziness needs a doctor's review before we do any hands-on neck work.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Plan: I'm holding manual neck work today. I'm referring you back to your doctor this week about the dizziness and the pinky tingling.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Ask your doctor directly about driving. For now, avoid long drives.

expectedFacts.statement: Neck pain 6 out of 10 on the left, worse turning to check mirrors
Dizziness on standing, twice this week
Driving is hard, cannot look over shoulder
Dizziness needs a doctor's review before hands-on neck work
Refer back to doctor this week
